bullets.title: THE 14 SEPTEMBER LIMIT CHANGE LANDED TODAY — +25% PERMANENT OVER THE OLD STANDARD, REPLACING A TEMPORARY +50%, WHICH IS A ~17% CUT AGAINST WHAT WE HAD YESTERDAY
bullets.summary: The vendor's own wording: "Starting September 14, we're permanently raising standard weekly limits in Claude Code by 25% for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans. Until then, the current 50% increase will be in place." Both facts must be held together or the headline misleads in either direction. Baseline 100 -> temporary boost (in force since 13 May 2026) 150 -> new permanent floor 125. So it is genuinely a permanent increase against the pre-May standard AND simultaneously a ~17% reduction against the ceiling every fire of this report has actually been running under, which is why the trade press covered it as a cut (BleepingComputer). This is the closure of standing action (e) — the one item with an external deadline — which the third fire on 13 Sep closed "unmeasured" and this morning's fire listed as CLOSED without a number.
bullets.how: YES — and the honest accounting is that the deadline produced the number, not us: it arrived because the change shipped and was reported, not because anyone measured our consumption first. The consequence is cadence. This report fired three times on 13 September and twice today, and Lens fires up to three times daily, all against one weekly pool that just dropped ~17% from yesterday's level. Nobody has ever measured what one fire costs, so the multi-fire design cannot currently be defended or priced — and the lever is already named and still at default: CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS. The measurement is finally cheap because the denominator is now a published constant rather than a promotional one.

bullets.title: THE COWORK / DESKTOP CHANGELOG — THE MORNING FIRE'S DECLARED GAP — IS NOW READ END-TO-END, AND IT ANSWERS ONE STANDING CONFIG ITEM OUTRIGHT WHILE ADDING A THIRD CONFIG-LAYER PERMISSION ESCAPE
bullets.summary: This morning's bullet 4 reported this primary as NOT READ rather than assuming it unchanged; it was reachable this fire and was read in full. NEGATIVE RESULT FIRST: newest entry is still v1.52386.3 (2026-09-11), the cloud-migration retry-timing fix already covered — nothing on 12, 13 or 14 September, so "nothing shipped" now holds on BOTH Anthropic primaries for a fourth consecutive day, verified rather than presumed. Two findings in v1.52386.0 (2026-09-10) never covered here, both landing on the standing list. (i) coworkSessionRetentionDays IS REAL AND THE CONFIRM-UNSET ITEM IS ANSWERED: organization-set retention now exists for all three surfaces (chatSessionRetentionDays, coworkSessionRetentionDays, codeSessionRetentionDays), deleting idle sessions "along with their files" after 1-3650 days, and the load-bearing clause is "unset deletes nothing"; sessionRetentionHold exists as a legal hold. (ii) A THIRD PERMISSION-BOUNDARY ESCAPE FIXED IN THE CONFIG LAYER: "Fixed Claude Code's own settings on the device (a user's or project's settings file, or a managed-settings.json) being able to turn OpenTelemetry trace export back on after an administrator configured a collector with traces off." Also noted: coworkEgressAllowedHosts governs which hostnames the agent's tools may reach (the mechanism behind this session's own fetch-provenance refusals), and the deprecated client-certificate fallback setting stops being accepted 17 November 2026, warning from 3 November.
bullets.how: YES — the retention clause closes a standing CONFIG item on evidence rather than expiry: the trace-reading audit method that standing action (a) depends on is safe by default, because unset deletes nothing. And the OTEL override is the confused-deputy shape again in our own daily tool — a local settings file silently overriding an administrator's decision — joining the two 2.1.269 near-misses (!-prefixed deny rule leaking past its source; Bash(tee:*) covering paths outside the working dirs) as the incident log's first vendor-side rows. Three now, all in the permission/config layer, all found by reading changelogs TWICE.

bullets.title: DOCUSIGN'S MCP SERVER GOES GENERALLY AVAILABLE GLOBALLY ON 30 SEPTEMBER — AND THE DOCUSIGN CONNECTOR IN THIS SESSION IS SITTING UNAUTHORIZED RIGHT NOW
bullets.summary: Announced 4 September, GA 30 September: agreement intelligence and governed actions, powered by Docusign's Iris engine, callable natively from Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Slack and any MCP client, with account-level admin controls, global multi-region infrastructure and multilingual support. Docusign joins Salesforce and ServiceNow in putting a system of record behind MCP. THE FIRST-PARTY OBSERVATION THAT MAKES IT OURS: this very session lists plugin:legal:docusign among the MCP servers REQUIRING AUTHENTICATION before their tools can be used — the connector is already provisioned in The Construct and is simply unauthorized, so the GA date is not an abstraction, it is the date the thing already wired into this stack becomes fully supported. Second real dated deadline alongside Perplexity's Sonar endpoint retirement on 27 September.
bullets.how: YES — for B9 this is the proposal-and-contract seam: signage quotes and Lennar/builder agreements currently leave the agent's reach at the moment they need a signature, and a governed MCP action closes that gap without a human re-keying anything. For PRAGMA it is the more interesting half: systems of record are becoming agent-callable on PUBLISHED DATES, which is exactly the surface an AI-operator engagement is sold against, and "your agreements are now reachable by any MCP client with admin controls you choose" is a conversation a client will have this month whether or not we start it.

bullets.title: "NOTHING SHIPPED" SURVIVED A DIRECT CHALLENGE — AND THE AGGREGATOR FAILURE MODE ESCALATED AGAIN, THIS TIME TO MIS-ATTRIBUTING OLD FEATURES TO A DATE THAT HAD NO RELEASE
bullets.summary: The audit trail of this fire. The search layer reported, under today's date, that "Claude Code added new policy and skill diagnostics, larger inline output limits, and file-based subagent prompts" — which reads as a 14 September release and is not one. PRIMARY CHANGELOG READ END-TO-END: newest entry is still 2.1.270, dated 12 September 2026, one line. The features named are real but belong to 2.1.269 (11 Sep) and earlier: claude plugin eval, /output-style, bashEditDiffEnabled, OTEL_METRICS_INCLUDE_REPOSITORY, CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS. So the day's only genuine vendor change was a pricing/limits change that never appears in a changelog at all (bullet 1). TWO SPECIFICS SURFACED BY THE FALSE LEAD AND KEPT BECAUSE THEY ARE TRUE: /skill-doctor reports which loaded skills go unused and what they cost in context — precisely the ECONOMY column of standing action (c), still one unrun command against a ~130-file corpus; and --append-subagent-system-prompt-file reads a subagent system prompt FROM A FILE, i.e. prose-to-configuration shipping in the product. CATEGORIES REPORTED EMPTY RATHER THAN FILLED: arXiv returned only 2601-2606 papers already in scope or older (Meta Context Engineering, the agent-skills survey, SkillGenBench) — empty for the second consecutive fire; frontier models — nothing dated 13-14 Sep, the Gemini 3.8 Flash / GPT-6 Astra / Fable-Mythos 5.1 cluster remains 1-3 Sep; funding — NVIDIA/Perplexity still TALKS not a closed round, and the Cognition ($26B, late May) and Glean (Series F, $7.2B) figures returned are historical.
bullets.how: MAYBE — one line of substance: the kill list is no longer mostly stale DATES, it is MIS-ATTRIBUTED PROVENANCE, and the countermeasure is the one already in force — read the primary, and when the primary is silent, say so.

bullets.title: STANDING ACTIONS — DAY FOURTEEN, SECOND FIRE: THE COMPLETION COUNT IS NO LONGER ZERO, AND BOTH CLOSURES CAME FROM READING A PRIMARY RATHER THAN FROM DOING WORK
bullets.summary: Not news; this report's open decisions, re-checked at the second fire and for the first time SHORTER than the morning's list. CLOSED THIS FIRE — (e) CADENCE-COST, now MEASURED not lost: the denominator is public (bullet 1), permanent +25% over the pre-May standard, ~17% below the boost we ran under through 13 Sep; what remains is one division, now worth doing because the denominator stopped moving. CLOSED THIS FIRE — coworkSessionRetentionDays confirm-unset: answered at the primary, "unset deletes nothing" (bullet 2). CONFIG (still unwritten): maxEffortLevel; --system-prompt-snapshot off; CLAUDE_CODE_WORKFLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_AGENTS (keep low until (a) exists, now directly implicated by the limit cut); and (b) the four Entra MCP controls — EIGHTH asking, five lines, unwritten. ARTIFACT: (a) the incident log — rows = AgentAudit's ten lifecycle dimensions, security column = the eight requirements from arXiv 2609.00267, first rows now number SIX (the four DCR-failed connectors plus THREE vendor-side permission-layer near-misses: the !-rule and Bash(tee:*) from 2.1.269, and the OTEL-traces override added today); (c) skill-corpus audit — still URGENT on this morning's re-pricing (threat actors authoring skills; spoofed Claude Code installers), and today it gains its ECONOMY instrument by name: /skill-doctor, one command. READ: RFC 9449 (DPoP), RFC 8707 (audience binding), the body of arXiv 2609.00006. CARRIED: OPENROUTER_MODEL=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash on the credentialed executor; which dsh / ls ~/.dsh unrun since 13 Sep; the launchd seam between a possibly-cloud-migrated writing task and the Mac-resident com.hartley.pragma-daily shipping job. NEW DATED DEADLINES ON THE BOARD: Perplexity Sonar retirement 27 Sep, Docusign MCP GA 30 Sep, client-cert fallback setting rejected 17 Nov, DCR removal after summer 2027.
bullets.how: YES — and the shape of today's two closures deserves stating plainly rather than celebrating. Fourteen days at zero completions, and the two items that closed did so because someone else published a number and a sentence, not because the backlog was worked. That is a fair description of what this report is good at (reading primaries carefully, twice) and what it has never once done (cause a config file to be written). The one item that would test the difference is unchanged and is now at its eighth asking: five lines.

praxis_lesson: TWO STANDING ACTIONS CLOSED TODAY AND NEITHER ONE WAS WORKED — THEY CLOSED BECAUSE A DEADLINE PASSED AND A VENDOR WROTE A SENTENCE. (e) got its number because the limit change shipped and the trade press did the arithmetic; the retention item got its answer because a changelog contained the clause "unset deletes nothing." Both are real closures and both are evidence about the process rather than achievements in it: after fourteen days, this report's completion mechanism is other people's publishing schedules. The item that would falsify that reading — (b), five lines of configuration, now at the eighth asking — remains exactly where it was on day one. SECOND LESSON, AND IT IS THE ONE WITH TEETH: READING CHANGELOGS IS NECESSARY AND INSUFFICIENT. Both Anthropic primaries were read end-to-end and both were quiet — fourth straight day — yet the single most consequential vendor change in a week landed today and APPEARS IN NO CHANGELOG AT ALL, because a weekly-limit change is pricing, not a release. A scan whose vendor surface is "the changelog" will systematically miss every change to cost, quota, terms and availability, which for an ecosystem billed by consumption is the category most likely to hurt. The fix is a source, not a resolution: watch the vendor's ANNOUNCEMENT channel alongside its release notes. THIRD LESSON, ON THE HONESTY LEDGER, BECAUSE IT PAID OUT TODAY: this morning's fire reported the Cowork changelog as NOT READ instead of assuming it unchanged; this fire read it and found two things sitting there since 10 September — the retention clause that closed a standing item, and a third config-layer permission escape. A gap recorded as a gap is a work item; a gap papered over is a false negative that never gets revisited. And the day's aggregator catch is the same discipline pointed outward: the search layer packaged 2.1.269's features as a 14 September release, which the dateline rule alone would NOT have caught, because the date was today and the PROVENANCE was wrong. Verify the figure, verify the date — and now verify that the feature belongs to the version the date claims.
